en: The Apadāna of the Elder Pañcahatthiya Upāli Chapter, Number 5 [Verse 1] When I was a merchant in the city of Benares, I saw the Buddha, the Teacher, the One with Vision, who had arrived at the gate of the city. [Verse 2] Having seen the Buddha, the Blessed One, I took five elephants and offered them to him. [Verse 3] I gave those five elephants to the Teacher, the One with Vision; having performed that meritorious deed, I passed away from that human existence. [Verse 4] Through that root of merit, I was reborn in the world of the gods; for eighty-four thousand aeons I dwelt in the realm of the Thirty-Three. [Verse 5] From there I passed away and was reborn in the human world; for eighty-four thousand aeons I was a wheel-turning monarch. [Verse 6] In every birth I possessed five elephants; by means of this very vehicle, I have reached the state of an Arhat. [Verse 7] I am now an Arhat, free from all defilements; having attained the goal, I dwell in peace, cooled and liberated. [Verse 8] I have lived the holy life and accomplished my task; I have laid down the burden and attained my own goal. Through the destruction of craving, I am liberated.

[Verse 9] My birth is ended, the holy life has been lived, what was to be done has been done, and there is no further state of existence beyond this. [Verse 10] I remember my former birth as a merchant in Benares; I recall offering five elephants to the Teacher, the One with Vision. [Verse 11] By the power of that merit, I have attained the fruit of Arhatship; I have reached the state of Arhatship and am established in the supreme security. [Verse 12] I have lived the holy life and accomplished my task; I have laid down the burden and attained my own goal. Through the destruction of craving, I am liberated. [Verse 13] My birth is ended, the holy life has been lived, what was to be done has been done, and there is no further state of existence beyond this. [Verse 14] This is the true Dharma, this is the true Vinaya, this is the true Teaching of the Buddha; I have realized it through my own direct knowledge and have become an Arhat. [Verse 15] I am one who has crossed over the flood, one who has reached the further shore; I am a sage who has transcended all states of existence and is released from the bonds of Māra. [Verse 16] I am a field of merit for the world, worthy of offerings and hospitality; I am a supreme vessel for gifts, and I am one who brings peace to the world. [Verse 17] I am a refuge for the world, a protector, and a shelter; I am a lamp for the world and a light for those wandering in darkness. [Verse 18] I am a leader for the world, a guide, and a teacher; I am a caravan leader for the world, leading beings across the great ocean of saṃsāra. [Verse 19] I am a physician for the world, a healer of the sick; I am a remover of the arrow of suffering for the world, and I am a bringer of peace. [Verse 20] I am a boatman for the world, ferrying beings across the river of existence; I am a pilot for the world, leading them to the island of nirvāṇa. [Verse 21] I am a sun for the world, dispelling the darkness of ignorance; I am a moon for the world, cooling the fever of the defilements. [Verse 22] I am a fire for the world, burning away the fuel of craving; I am a wind for the world, blowing away the dust of pride. [Verse 23] I am a mountain for the world, immovable and firm; I am an ocean for the world, deep and unfathomable. [Verse 24] I am a tree for the world, providing shade for all; I am a jewel for the world, rare and precious. [Verse 25] I am a lion for the world, fearless and powerful; I am an elephant for the world, mighty and steadfast. [Verse 26] I am a bull for the world, leading the herd of disciples; I am a horse for the world, swift and noble. [Verse 27] I am a charioteer for the world, driving the chariot of the Dharma; I am a warrior for the world, victorious over the army of Māra. [Verse 28] I am a king for the world, ruling with the Dharma; I am a sovereign for the world, protecting all beings. [Verse 29] I am a father for the world, nurturing all with compassion; I am a mother for the world, providing sustenance through the Dharma. [Verse 30] I am a friend for the world, never abandoning anyone; I am a relative for the world, always present in times of need. [Verse 31] I am a teacher for the world, instructing in the path to liberation; I am a preceptor for the world, ordaining disciples into the holy life. [Verse 32] I am a counselor for the world, advising on the way to peace; I am a guide for the world, showing the path to the city of nirvāṇa. [Verse 33] I am a benefactor for the world, bestowing the gift of the Dharma; I am a giver of happiness for the world, bringing joy to all beings. [Verse 34] I am a source of light for the world, illuminating the darkness of delusion; I am a vessel of truth for the world, upholding the Dharma. [Verse 35] I am a treasury for the world, filled with the jewels of wisdom; I am a mine of virtue for the world, extracting the gems of moral conduct. [Verse 36] I am a bridge for the world, spanning the chasm of saṃsāra; I am a ladder for the world, ascending to the heights of enlightenment. [Verse 37] I am a raft for the world, crossing the ocean of suffering; I am a boat for the world, sailing to the shore of safety. [Verse 38] I am a medicine for the world, healing the wounds of the defilements; I am a spell for the world, casting out the demons of passion. [Verse 39] I am a sword for the world, cutting through the net of doubt; I am a shield for the world, protecting against the arrows of Māra. [Verse 40] I am a fortress for the world, impregnable to the attacks of evil; I am a citadel for the world, secure from all fear. [Verse 41] I am a jewel for the world, rare and difficult to find;

I am a treasure for the world, inexhaustible and eternal. [Verse 42] I am a wish-fulfilling gem for the world, granting the desires of the faithful; I am a cloud for the world, raining down the nectar of the Dharma. [Verse 43] I am a spring for the world, flowing with the water of wisdom; I am a lake for the world, reflecting the beauty of the Truth. [Verse 44] I am a lotus for the world, pure and unstained by the mud of existence; I am a bee for the world, sipping the honey of the Dharma. [Verse 45] I am a garland for the world, adorning the heads of the virtuous; I am a perfume for the world, filling the air with the scent of renunciation. [Verse 46] I am a song for the world, singing the praises of liberation; I am a dance for the world, performing the steps of peace. [Verse 47] I am a feast for the world, satisfying the hunger of seekers; I am a banquet for the world, feasting on the food of the Dharma. [Verse 48] I am a festival for the world, celebrating the victory over death; I am a jubilee for the world, rejoicing in the attainment of nirvāṇa. [Verse 49] I am a victory for the world, triumphant over all adversaries; I am a triumph for the world, exulting in the conquest of Māra. [Verse 50] I am a blessing for the world, bringing prosperity to all; I am a boon for the world, granting the gift of peace. [Verse 51] I am a gift for the world, bestowed upon the needy; I am a favor for the world, shown to all without distinction. [Verse 52] I
“The Fully Enlightened One named Sumedha was walking through the marketplace;
with eyes cast downward, he spoke in measured tones.”
Mindful and with senses restrained,
they brought five handfuls of blue lotuses for me to wear as a garland.
With that, full of faith, I honored the Buddha with my own hands;
and those flowers were offered.
They covered the Teacher with tears;
they concentrated upon the Great Elephant as disciples do for their teacher.
In the thirty thousand aeons that followed when I offered that flower,
I did not know a state of misery.
This is the fruit of worshiping the Buddha.
Twenty hundred kalpas from now,
there will be five kṣatriyas;
Named Hatthiya by name,
he was a mighty wheel-turning monarch.
He possessed the four analytical knowledges (paṭisambhidā).
the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed did the Venerable Pañcahatthiya Thera speak these verses.
The legend of the Elder Pañcahatthiya is the fifth.
